costGuide.title: Volkswagen DADA Engine Replacement Cost
paragraphs: Understanding the DADA engine replacement cost requires looking at supply-only pricing versus fitted costs. The DADA is a highly common unit across the VW Group, meaning supply costs remain competitive across the UK.
Ancillaries: Quotes including the alternator, starter motor, and injectors will sit at the higher end of the band.
Warranty: A 12-month unlimited mileage warranty typically adds £100-£150 to the supply cost compared to a standard 3-month warranty.
VAT: Consumer quotes are typically VAT-inclusive, but B2B quotes may vary.
For a detailed breakdown of pricing across all Volkswagen engines, see the Volkswagen engine prices guide .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the DADA
variants.intro: The 1.0 TSI family uses multiple engine codes that share the same physical block but differ in ECU mapping, turbocharger specification, and emissions equipment. Fitting the wrong revision will trigger ECU faults and potentially fail an MOT emissions test. 1. VW Data Label: Located in the engine bay (often on the inner wing or strut tower) or in the boot under the carpet. The code is printed in the bottom right corner of the data sticker.

relatives.code: Predecessor: VW EA111 1.2 TSI / 1.4 TSI (e.g., CZCA / CZDA)**
relatives.description: The DADA directly replaced the problematic EA111 timing-chain-driven small petrol engines. Unlike its predecessor, the DADA uses a quieter, more reliable timing belt and an integrated exhaust manifold for faster warm-up.

Introduced around 2020, the EA211 evo family features updated engine management, a slightly revised turbocharger, and a higher compression ratio. While physically similar, the evo variants are not a direct plug-and-play swap for a DADA without ECU remapping and loom modifications.

Sharing the same 999cc block, the CHZD produces 115PS compared to the DADA’s 95PS. The CHZD uses a larger turbocharger and different intercooler plumbing. Attempting to swap a CHZD into a DADA vehicle will trigger boost-related fault codes and require significant hardware changes.

relatives.code: Cross-Brand Twin: SEAT / Škoda 1.0 TSI (CHZB / CHZD)**
relatives.description: The exact same EA211 architecture is used across SEAT (Ibiza, Arona) and Škoda (Fabia, Scala, Kamiq). While the core block is identical, always verify the engine code sticker, as minor differences in ancillary bracket mounting or ECU calibration can exist between VW, SEAT, and Škoda applications.

variants.closing: 2. V5C Logbook: Check the "Engine Number" section, though this often lists the serial number rather than the code. 3. Under the Bonnet Sticker: Some later models have a dedicated sticker on the slam panel. Confusable Sibling Codes DGJA: 1.0 TSI 95PS. Physically identical to the DADA but features updated ECU software and slightly different emissions calibration. DKRA: 1.0 TSI 115PS. Features a larger turbocharger and different intercooler plumbing. Not a direct swap. DRVA: 1.0 TSI 95PS. Later revision with an updated oil pump and timing belt tensioner. If you are sourcing a replacement DADA engine, ensure the supplier guarantees the exact code. A DKRA unit will physically bolt in, but the ECU and turbo plumbing will not match without significant modification.

buyingGuide.title: Volkswagen DADA Buying Guide

options.label: Used
options.body: A used DADA engine (£500-£1,000 ) is a viable option if the donor vehicle has low mileage and a documented water pump replacement. However, without a warranty on the water pump and turbo, you inherit the same failure risks. Explore used Volkswagen engines .

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: The reconditioned DADA (£1,200-£2,200 ) is the most popular choice. A proper reconditioning process replaces the timing belt, water pump, tensioners, and validates the turbocharger. This addresses the engine's primary weak points and offers the best balance of cost and reliability. Compare reconditioned Volkswagen engines .

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A rebuilt DADA (£2,000-£3,500 ) involves stripping the block to bare metal, machining the cylinder head and block, and replacing all internal bearings and seals. This is only recommended if the original DADA suffered catastrophic failure (e.g., timing belt snap causing valve damage). View rebuilt Volkswagen engines .

items.question: How much does a reconditioned Volkswagen DADA 1.0 TSI engine cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Volkswagen DADA engine typically costs between £1,200 and £2,200 for supply-only . This price band reflects a unit that has had the known weak points (water pump, timing belt, and turbocharger) addressed, offering the best balance of reliability and value for this specific code.

items.question: What are the most common failures of the Volkswagen DADA engine?
items.answer: The two most documented failure patterns for the DADA are plastic water pump/thermostat housing leaks (typically appearing between 80k-120k miles) and carbon buildup on the direct-injection intake valves. Both are well-understood issues; if caught early, they are inexpensive to repair, but ignored coolant loss can lead to catastrophic overheating requiring a full Volkswagen DADA engine replacement.

items.question: Can I fit a CHZD or DGJA engine in place of my failed DADA?
items.answer: Physically, the blocks will bolt into the same chassis mounts. However, the CHZD (115PS) and DGJA (EA211 evo) feature different turbochargers, intercooler plumbing, and ECU calibrations. Fitting one without swapping the corresponding loom, turbo, and ECU will result in persistent fault codes, poor drivability, and a failed MOT emissions test. Always source an exact-code DADA replacement.

items.question: How long does it take to replace a Volkswagen DADA engine?
items.answer: Independent UK specialists typically quote 6 to 8 hours of labour for a Volkswagen DADA engine removal and refit (R&R). This translates to a typical fitted labour premium of £390 to £520 , depending on regional labour rates and whether ancillary components (like the alternator or AC compressor) are transferred or replaced.

items.question: Is it worth replacing the engine in a VW Polo or Golf with a DADA code?
items.answer: Yes. The typical UK market value for a DADA-equipped Volkswagen Polo or Golf ranges from £3,000 to £12,000 . A reconditioned Volkswagen DADA engine replacement cost sits comfortably within this value band, making it a financially sound repair. However, if your specific vehicle is at the very bottom of this value range, you should evaluate its scrap or part-exchange value before committing to the repair.
